messages:
emma: heads-up, PR #412 keeps hitting flaky failures in the GH Actions eval workflow. looks like the python venv install step is timing out intermittently and cache misses are frequent.

emma: failing log excerpt:
```
ERROR: Could not build wheels for sentencepiece which use PEP 517 and cannot be installed directly
Install pip wheel: subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['python', '-m', 'pip', 'wheel', '--no-deps', '-w', '/tmp/pip-wheel-...']' timed out after 300s
```

raj: ugh. i've seen this when runners spin up cold and network is slow. we should either warm a cache or move heavy deps to a prebuilt artifact.

sasha: agree. options: 1) add a warmup job that restores wheel/artifact from previous nightly and populate ~/.cache/pip 2) switch the heavy eval jobs to our self-hosted runners that have preinstalled wheels 3) increase timeout + retry wrapper.

emma: preference toward 1 + 3 for quick fix. can we pin python & pip versions too? some builds vary and break the wheel builds.

matt: pinning makes sense. also recommend using actions/cache with key: venv-pip-${{ matrix.python-version }}-sha-${{ hashFiles('**/pyproject.toml') }} to reduce misses. but cache restore sometimes fails on first run (cold). hence warmup job.

raj: warmup job idea (pseudo):
```yaml
jobs:
  warmup-pip-cache:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Restore pip cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: venv-pip-${{ runner.os }}-{{ matrix.python-version }}-stable
      - name: Prebuild wheels
        run: python -m pip wheel -r ci/eval-requirements.txt -w /tmp/wheels || true
      - name: Upload wheels
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: wheels-nightly
          path: /tmp/wheels
```

sasha: and then eval jobs can download-artifact wheels-nightly before pip install. avoids network and build.

ci-bot: :warning: nightly-evals cron job failed to complete last night (exit 1). artifact upload step timed out after 10m.

emma: we should also add exponential retry wrapper around pip install to handle transient network flakiness. simple bash wrapper: retry 3 times with sleep backoff.

matt: also consider moving some heavy packages (sentencepiece, tokenizers) into a prebuilt docker image used by GH Actions for evals. image would be updated nightly and reduce build time drastically. tradeoff: heavier image publishing infra.

raj: For PR gating specifically, we can gate small smoke evals on GH Actions (fast, cached) and route full evals to buildkite or dedicated runners. keep gating cheap but indicative.

olga: i can prototype the warmup -> download-artifact flow. will add a small manifest check so eval jobs bail early if artifact fails to download and fallback to 'build-from-source' path with retries.

emma: thanks. olga, can you also add a lightweight metric in the workflow that records install time to our metrics endpoint? even a simple curl to internal collector. will help tune thresholds.

olga: yep. plan:
- add warmup job that runs nightly + on merge to main
- upload wheels artifact
- eval jobs attempt download; if fail, run pip --use-pep517 build with retries
- add install_time metric (curl POST JSON)

sasha: for immediate PR pain, i'm going to increase the job timeout from 10m -> 20m and add 2 retries. that should reduce noise until we get warmup + docker image.

matt: small note: make sure to set concurrency on nightly so we don't stomp cache from parallel runs. key: nightly-evals-${{ github.ref }}.

emma: great. can we also add a canary job that runs the warmup on a self-hosted runner once per day to validate artifact integrity? if that passes we mark nightly as healthy.

raj: +1. final ask: update PR gating docs (devex repo) with new expectations: "fast-smoke only; full-eval runs in buildkite or nightly; if PR needs full-eval trigger, request via /eval-bot". avoid people relying on GH Actions for heavy workloads.

olga: i'll open a PR with the workflow changes in ~2 hours and ping here.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: apply/ci-workflows v0.4.1 -> staging at 2026-03-20T15:02:00Z

emma: perfect. thanks everyone :rocket:
